### The Downward Spiral of Sin
Author: Alistair Begg
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-may-23-2023.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 11:2-3
Points:
- Sin advances by subtle degrees rather than happening all at once.
- David neglected his duties as king by staying home alone instead of leading his army.
- An accidental glance turned into a deliberate and lingering gaze.
- Lust overpowered David's moral sense, ignoring that Bathsheba was another man's wife.
- Spiritual complacency leaves anyone vulnerable to falling, but God always provides a way out.

### Get Off the Roof!
Author: Jill Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-women/get-off-the-roof-one-year-devotions-for-women-february-10.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 11:2
Points:
- Even dedicated and mature believers remain vulnerable to moral failure.
- Idleness and lack of discipline placed David in the path of temptation.
- Adultery starts in the eyes and mind before taking physical shape.
- A lingering initial look easily leads to repeated glances and full compromise.
- Believers must actively flee compromising environments instead of remaining near danger.

### A Seductive Glow
Author: Stuart Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/a-seductive-glow-one-year-devotions-for-men-october-23.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 11:1-2
Points:
- Temptation offers an opportunity either to fall or to develop spiritual integrity.
- David’s failure was preceded by gradual spiritual carelessness and indiscipline.
- While David could not control the first glance, he was responsible for gazing and acting on lust.
- Ignoring basic spiritual safeguards turns even strong men into moral weaklings.
- Flirting with temptation is like a moth circling a flame until it is destroyed.

### David’s Great Sin
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/davids-great-sin
Passage: 2 Samuel 11:2
Points:
- Even a godly king after God's own heart remains prone to severe moral failure.
- David allowed lust to override his conscience, leading to adultery and murder.
- An initial compromise created a destructive cycle of deception and cover-up.
- God graciously breaks through spiritual blindness and confronts hidden sin.
- True devotion to God is demonstrated by genuine repentance when confronted with failure.
